newsitem.title: USA: Quaker launches oat ads after FDA ruling.
newsitem.headline: Quaker launches oat ads after FDA ruling.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co. wasted no time in taking advantage of a government ruling that advertising the health benefits of oats is okay.
Its advertising campaign will start Wednesday.
Quaker, which accounts for about 75 percent of the U.S. oatmeal market, got the good news Tuesday when the Food and Drug Administration said it would allow such advertising.
The FDA said it would allow companies that make foods containing soluble fiber from whole oats to claim that eating these foods may reduce the risk of heart disease.
"We're going to be very aggressive about educating consumers," Bruce Poole, director of marketing for Quaker Oatmeal, said in a telephone interview.
Poole said Quaker's oatmeal and cold cereal that contain oat fiber will be featured in newspaper advertising starting Wednesday. Television advertising will follow in a few days.
Since January 1996, when the FDA said it was considering such a rule, oatmeal sales rose about 5 percent, Poole said.
"We see that trend continuing if not accelerating," he added.
To qualify for the health claims, the FDA said a product must be made from whole oats, be low in saturated fat and cholestrol and have a minimum of 0.75 grams of soluble fiber per serving.
Among Quaker products that qualify are rolled oats and most instant oatmeals, as well as cold cereals like its Oat Bran Cereal, Quaker Toasted Oatmeal and Quaker Oatmeal Squares.
Poole said Quaker expects to redesign its packages to include the FDA health claim within six to eight weeks.
